claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'EVALUATE statement, VI-84' followed by the indented sub-entry 'Conditional expression, VI-54'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'EVALUATE statement, VI-84' then '  Conditional expression, VI-54'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost when rendered (pages 961-962 use nested '- ' list items and keep them). Index is informative; the entry text and page references themselves match the PDF.

verdict.reasoning: The 300-dpi render of page 966 (B-54, informative Index) shows a two-column list of entries, sub-entries indented under their main entry, continuation lines (e.g. 'X-34, XIII-76' under ERROR PROCEDURES) also indented. The markdown page-966.md holds the same entries in the same order, one per line, with sub-entries and continuations indented by two spaces; the entry text and page references match (the claim itself concedes this). The source text preserves every entry boundary and the indentation hierarchy line for line; the only difference is that the transcription uses bare indented lines rather than '- ' list markup, so a Markdown renderer would reflow them. That is a formatting/markup convention, not a content discrepancy: nothing is missing, misquoted or changed in meaning, and the page is informative index furniture. Consistency with pages 961-962 is a style matter.
